MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, JUNE 4, 2025

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its meeting on
Wednesday, June 4, 2025, in the Council Chambers on the ninth floor
of City Hall. Following the Pledge of Allegiance by Commissioner
Rice, the meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Commissioner Carolyn Fowler
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aidé Trejo
  Chairman Larry Springs
Excused
Absence:  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams

Staff:  Bernard McCrumby, Jr., Planning Manager
  Michael Pan, Assistant City Attorney
  Arturo Salazar, Senior Planner
  Christine Rivera, Senior Planner
  Angel Leon-Martell, Planner
  Sean May, Planner
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary

(3)  STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Mr. McCrumby stated:
1. Addressing the fact that there is a Typo in the Agenda page,
page one, date of the Minutes for approval, correction made, copies
distributed.
2. Inglewood will serve as the host city for the Destination Market
Street Informational Workshop on Monday, June 9, 2025, with PCR
Business Finance Corp.
3. Item 6E – pushed forward to the July 2, 2025, Meeting.
4. Items 6B and 6C will be presented together tonight.

approve the staff request.

approve all of Staff’s requests, and Commissioner Fowler seconded
it.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Fowler, Rice, Trejo, and Chairman Springs.

(4)  PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None.

Childress representing Strips n’ Dips for Special Use Permit No. 25-
00005 (SUP25-00005) to allow the sale of beer, wine, and distilled
spirits for on-site consumption for an existing fast-food restaurant
on an H-C (Historic Core) zoned property at 128 North Market Street.

Before Staff’s presentation, Commissioner Rice recused himself from
the dais, as item 6A is one of his clients.

Mr. Sean May, Planner, made the staff presentation.

The Chairman asked the  Planning  Commission  if  there  were  any
questions for the staff.

Commissioner Fowler asked staff –
• Was there a reason that the Police Reporting statistics could not
  be for the current year of 2025 for data incidents within the
  area?
  - Mr. May responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
• Asked why this item was continued to this month’s Planning
  Commission meeting?
• Why didn’t staff continue this item until they had received the
  current 2025 Crime statistics information?
  - Mr. May responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions
  - Mr. McCrumby responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

Chairman Springs asked the staff –
• What is the minimum/maximum licenses within a census tract?
  - Mr. May responded to Chairman Springs’ question.

The Chairman asked the applicant to come forward to address the
Planning Commission.

Ms. Keokia Childress, representing Strips and Dip, and Mr. Brandon
Williams, Supervisor of Wait-Staff, Bartenders, and Door Security
staff of Strips and Dip.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for the Planning Commission to
question the applicant.

Commissioner Fowler asked the applicant –
• What is the actual name of the Business?
• What is the seating capacity?
• What type of meals are served?
• I.D. training, how to spot fake IDs, and what is the recourse for
  showing a fake ID?
• Security is supplied for both entrances of the restaurant.
  - Ms. Childress responded to Commissioner Fowler’s questions.
  - Mr. Williams responded to Commissioner Fowler’s question.

  2

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant –
• How are Alcohol sales conducted? Is the customer only allowed to
  order from the menu of drinks, or can they also order from the
  wall display of distilled spirits?
• Who will be the security on duty?
• Who will handle the ID, and how will it be handled?
  - Ms. Childress responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.
  - Mr. Williams responded to Commissioner Trejo’s questions.

favor of or against this project.

FOR / AGAINST:
1. Lashanda Lambert, Inglewood Resident - For

Planning Commission.

Commissioner Trejo motioned to affirm the Categorical Exemption EA-
CE-2025-038 and adopt the resolution approving SUP25-00005, along
with these added conditions of approval: 1. One year review by the
Planning Commission of the business, 2. No Loitering Signs posted at
the front and rear of the building, 3. Steps need to be taken and
followed according to the Design Review Standards, Section 4. Steps
taken to reach out and connect with the Inglewood Police Department,
5. Food is readily available and made fresh, 6. All alcohol orders
from the Menu, not from the wall display, and was seconded by
Commissioner Fowler, Resolution No. 2026

Chairman Springs asked if the Planning Commission had any questions
for the applicant.

Commissioner Fowler asked the applicant –
• Security on site – I understand that there are cameras, but if
  there is a need for assistance and no live person is on site?
• Do you have more parking spaces? I see that the size of your
  facility should have at least 71 parking spaces, but you are
  requesting fewer. How many customers do you see daily that would
  allow you to reduce the number of parking spaces?
  - Mr. Henry responded to Commissioner Fowler’s questions.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant –
• Are you the original owner who came before this planning
  commission a couple of years ago when we approved this site for
  storage?
  - Mr. Henry responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.

•  How soon will it take for you to be up and running if this project
  is approved, for full business operations?
  - Mr. Henry responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.

  - Mr. Henry responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.
•  Are you able to track or know who is at the facility during
  business hours?
  - Mr. Henry responded to Commissioner Rice’s question.

Commissioner Trejo asked the applicant –
• If someone in the facility has a medical emergency, do you have
  the ability to watch live what is going on, or are you only able
  to watch through your cameras? How do you handle this situation,
  and will you be able to assist the individual?
  - Mr. Henry responded to Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Chairman Springs asked the staff and the applicant –
• How many 71 parking spaces need to be approved? Now, the previous
  building was only approved for 10 parking spaces, so why is this
  project being approved for 16? Why would the Planning Commission
  approve such a small number of parking spaces, yet require a large
  number of parking spaces? Why, and what would those additional
  spaces be used for?
  - Mr. Henry responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
  - Mr. May responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
  - Mr. McCrumby responded to Chairman Springs’ question.
